newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse seen capped by heavy primary offer.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse seen capped by heavy primary offer.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse is unlikely to break away from its sideways drift, in which the market has remained since mid-March with investors focused on large and attractive primary market offers, analysts said.

Some said the bourse could rise in the beginning of the week rebounding after its total 4.5-percent falls late last week and earlier this week but said the upside was limited and expected it to extend its 12-week flat trend. @

"The possible growth is likely to be brief...we are still in a sideways drift and we are likely to return to the middle (of the channel), I think we will be in the flat trend until polls," said Roman Sosnowski of Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market all-share WIG index fell 1.5 percent this week to 15,941.7 points on Friday.
Some analysts said the zloty strengthening after a two-percent fall earlier in the week, triggered by the Czech crown slump, was a positive signal, but was unlikely to spur strong gains. @
"It's good it (the zloty fall) is finished as it caused some nervousness on the market, but I don't think it's such a strong signal for the bourse," said Kamil Kalemba of ING Baring Securities.

Analysts said the bourse was likely to be still influenced by the busy primary market, where Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA was offering shares worth one billion zlotys and by forthcoming polls due in September keeping many investors on the sidelines. @
Hausehold appliances maker Amica Wronki SA started its initial public offering worth 110 million zlotys on Friday and copper giant KGHM was likely to start its offer in June.
Analysts said, however, no major selling was likely at current prices as stocks looked attractive with average price earnings ratio of 15.5.
Analysts said Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw might get additional boost early next week, after Friday's news they have removed main obstacles to their planned merger. @
They said, however, the market had already discounted the merger news and any gains were likely to be limited.
Analysts said Handlowy's and KGHM's bourse entry seen in mid-year could help the bourse attract new capital in longer-term by boosting the exchange's capitalisation and liquidity.
ZEW was the market's top gainer this week, rising 32.8 percent after it started bourse trade on Monday, 20 percent below its issue price. @
Construction and trading firm Atlantis SA starts bourse trade on Wednesday next week.
